actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository holds MJCF description files for OpenArm v2, Cell, v1 and v0.3 simulation in MuJoCo
The README's v1 bimanual launch command opens v1/scene.xml with the home keyframe
The v1 scene is the MJCF model 'openarm_bimanual scene' and includes openarm_bimanual.xml from the same directory
The included bimanual model sets the integration step to 0.001 s and the implicitfast integrator
The actuator section declares 16 position actuators: eight per arm (seven arm joints and one finger)
The motor_finger default class gives the finger position actuators the control range -0.005 to 0.044 m
The left arm's first joint is the hinge openarm_left_joint1 with the range -3.490659 to 1.396263 rad
The right arm's first joint is the hinge openarm_right_joint1 with the range -1.396263 to 3.490659 rad
The left hand has two slide finger joints, openarm_left_finger_joint1 and openarm_left_finger_joint2, with the range 0 to 0.044 m
The right hand has the matching pair of slide finger joints, openarm_right_finger_joint1 and openarm_right_finger_joint2, also with the range 0 to 0.044 m
The two fingers of each hand are coupled by an equality constraint
The model provides a home keyframe with 18 qpos values (nine per arm) and 16 ctrl values (eight per arm)
The package requires Python 3.10 or newer and depends on mujoco 3.6.0 or newer and numpy
The upstream launcher loads a model with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path and creates its data with mujoco.MjData
The launcher hands the model to mujoco.viewer.launch unless --static is given; static mode calls mj_forward without stepping

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element, so the same ctrl sequence and tick count repeat the trajectory.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses v1/scene.xml and its included v1/openarm_bimanual.xml for the 1 ms step, the 18 qpos and 18 dof coordinates and the 16 actuator ctrlranges, then moves each actuated joint toward its control target; it computes no inertias, contacts, tendons, finger equalities or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
the meshes and textures under v1/meshes are not loaded by the stand-in; a real engine load needs them beside the scene, which the pinned clone provides

the bridge's reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults (zero qpos in the stand-in), not from the home keyframe of v1/openarm_bimanual.xml:566-572; a client that wants that pose must send the keyframe ctrl and step

no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's 1 ms step only; the upstream launcher's non-static viewer owns real-time pacing (src/openarm_mujoco/v2/launch.py:114-116), which this package does not use
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the model's sensor section is not exposed as an observation, only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is
the model is a simulation asset for OpenArm: no physical arm is modelled or controlled and nothing here was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the world state stays readable
